label: Fixed initial history and possibility transfer: inclusion edge and frugality assessed
summary: Composed FixedInitial535 History with PossibilityTransfer. Four-history equivalence-frame model: a same-description, different-initial-bearer history and a different-description history are E-possible but not M-possible under the rigid reading; the qualitative reading admits bearer omission and gives no necessary bearer. Restricted inclusion on one description's witnesses suffices for its transfer and is strictly weaker than full inclusion; for a complete history description transfer is equivalent to one access edge. Rigid preservation, an E-admissible bearer omission and restricted inclusion are jointly inconsistent; rigid plus full inclusion makes the initial bearer E-necessary. Re-read pinned Oppy 2020 §I p.14 (strong sentence) and §VI pp.19-20 (case-wise de dicto / this initial state / part-or-aspect readings). Frugality (Oppy 2013, navigation only) is a comparative theory-choice reason, not a definitional exclusion; its force needs an unsupplied rule counting possibilities rather than necessities as commitments, and against theism Oppy's own §VI supports parity. Practice treating initial conditions as explanatory targets supports E-admissibility only. Rejected: conceivability alone refutes fixed history; origin essentialism forces or forbids alternative starts. Full assessment in docs/notes/fixed-initial-history-535.md, section Issue #1588.
blocker: No warranted account of metaphysical access for initial histories: the restricted inclusion for bearer-omitting histories is the discriminating premise and remains open; Oppy's part-or-aspect case needs its own inclusion edge; no accounting rule for modal commitments is defended. Independent semantic challenge pending.
